question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2}$ that satisfies $y(-5)=1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+1 \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\text{d}y & =\int \frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+\int \,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{y} & =-\frac{1}{(x + 4)}+(x + 4)+C \\ \frac{1}{y} & =\frac{1-{(x + 4)}^{2}-C(x + 4)}{(x + 4)} \\ y & =\frac{(x + 4)}{1-{(x + 4)}^{2}-C(x + 4)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{(x + 4)}{1-{(x + 4)}^{2}-C(x + 4)},\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the initial condition $y(-5)=1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-5) & =1 \\ \frac{-1}{1-(-1)^{2}-C(-1)} & =1 \\ \frac{-1}{C} & =1 \\ C & =-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{(x + 4)}^{2}}+{y}^{2}$ that satisfies the condition $y(-5)=1$ is

$$
y=\frac{(x + 4)}{1+(x + 4)-{(x + 4)}^{2}}\,.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{3}$ that satisfies $y(-2)=\frac{1}{8}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={y}^{2}(3{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{(x + 4)}^{3}) \\ \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =3{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{(x + 4)}^{3} \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (3{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{(x + 4)}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\ \int \frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =3\int {(x + 4)}^{2}\,\text{d}x-4\int {(x + 4)}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{y} & ={(x + 4)}^{3}-{(x + 4)}^{4}+C \\ y & =\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{4}-{(x + 4)}^{3}-C}.\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(-2)=\frac{1}{8}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-2) & =\frac{1}{8} \\ \frac{1}{{2}^{4}-{2}^{3}-C} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ \frac{1}{8-C} & =\frac{1}{8} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{2}-4{y}^{2}{(x + 4)}^{3}$ that satisfies the condition $y(-2)=\frac{1}{8}$ is

$$
y=\frac{1}{{(x + 4)}^{4}-{(x + 4)}^{3}}\,.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)$ that satisfies $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})={\pi }^{2}.$ Assume that $0<(x + 4)<\pi .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We first find the general solution and then apply the given initial condition to find a particular solution.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)+8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}+8(x + 4) \\ \int \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}+8(x + 4))\,\text{d}x \\ \int \,\text{d}y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x+8\int (x + 4)\,\text{d}x \\ y & =\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x+4{(x + 4)}^{2}+{C}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the integral on the right-hand side of this equality, we use a substitution

$$
u=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Then  we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+{C}_{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4))+{C}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

where we used that $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)>0.$

Hence,

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4))+4{(x + 4)}^{2}+C.
$$

where $C={C}_{1}+{C}_{2}$ is an arbitrary constant. 

We now apply the initial condition $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})={\pi }^{2}$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2}) & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})+4{\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)}^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡1+{\pi }^{2}+C & ={\pi }^{2} \\ C & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-8(x + 4)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x + 4)$ that satisfies the condition $y(-4 + \frac{\pi}{2})={\pi }^{2}$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x + 4))+4{(x + 4)}^{2}.
$$

\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x - 4)}^{3}-{(x - 4)}^{2}+C) \\ y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x - 4)}^{3}-{(x - 4)}^{2}+C)\end{aligned}
$$

We now apply the initial condition $y(5)=1$ to find $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y(5) & =1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3}-{1}^{2}+C) & =1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡C & =1 \\ C & =e\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the particular solution of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2(x - 4){e}^{-y}=3{(x - 4)}^{2}{e}^{-y}$ that satisfies the condition $y(5)=1$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡({(x - 4)}^{3}-{(x - 4)}^{2}+e).
$$
